title: Scale pathways QBR & tech elevation cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact QBR + expansion play cheat sheet for CS reps and solutions engineers who are preparing renewal conversations with an upsell motion (Dedicated capacity upgrades, Private deployment pilots, or premium SLA add-ons). The goal is to move from a health review to a clear, technical path for scale within the same meeting.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions / SEs supporting enterprise upsell conversations
- Sales engineering for pricing alignment

Status: DRAFT — use during customer QBRs; copy into customer-facing doc after review.

QBR agenda template (45–60m, compressible):
1) 0–5m Quick check-in & meeting objective (set expansion intent if appropriate)
2) 5–15m Health snapshot (usage, latency, errors, SLOs, token volume trend)
   - Top 3 metrics: avg p50/p95 latency, monthly token consumption, error rate by route
   - Call out anomalies (inc. infra incidents, model regressions)
3) 15–30m Business outcomes & roadmap alignment
   - Which product teams are using Redwood? (features, release cadence)
   - Business KPIs impacted by inference (engagement lift, conversion, automation throughput)
4) 30–45m Scale conversation (pick 1 primary path: Dedicated / Private / SLA)
   - Present 1–2 propositions (cost/latency ROI, delivery timeline, migration steps)
   - Technical lift & risks (SE drives details)
5) 45–60m Ask + next steps (decision owner, POC dates, contract contact)

Expansion signals (quick checklist to surface in QBR):
- Sustained utilization > 60% of shared-prod capacity for 4+ weeks OR rising p95 latency during peak
- Spike in concurrent requests leading to queueing on hosted tier
- Data governance requests (audit logs, VPC, KMS)
- SLA needs: legal/regulatory ask for uptime > 99.9% or financial penalties
- Predictable burst behavior (seasonal or campaign-driven)
- High per-token spend where quantization / batching could materially reduce costs

Qualification matrix (yes/no / evidence):
- Budget owner identified? (Y/N + name)
- Timeline for decision? (quarters)
- Security/compliance blockers? (list)
- Internal infra team bandwidth for Private pilot? (estimate FTE)
- Expected throughput after upgrade (tokens/sec, concurrency)

Playbook: Dedicated capacity upgrade (fast path)
- When to propose: customer needs predictable throughput and cost per token, or host tier shows sustained utilization > threshold.
- Key value props to lead with: predictable latency, reserved GPU capacity, burst credit for campaigns.
- Tech checklist for SE:
  1) Current model & peak memory usage (report: model_name, seq_len, peak_gpu_mem_gb)
  2) Actual concurrency and p95 latency during peak windows (time-windowed traces)
  3) Suggested pool size (gpus + instance types) and baseline throughput estimate
  4) Migration plan: routing policy change -> canary -> full cutover (example steps below)
  5) Fallback policy: auto-route to hosted-compatible variant if Dedicated pool unhealthy
- Example migration steps (canary):
  - Day 0: Provision pool (x GPUs), validate model variant and quantization profile in staging
  - Day 1: Canary 5–10% of traffic + SLO monitoring (1–2 business days)
  - Day 3: Ramp 50% with rollback window, validate cost/runbook
  - Day 5: Full route switch and decommission canary rules
- Commercial notes: include reserved commitment options (1/12/36 months), and add-on for extended observability

Playbook: Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) pilot
- When to propose: regulatory/compliance demand, strict data residency, or full control of infra.
- Typical customer ask: private control plane + data plane inside customer VPC or on-prem appliance.
- SE checklist:
  1) Compliance baseline: required certifications (SOC2, ISO, local regs)
  2) Network readiness: IP ranges, peering, egress rules, VPN / Direct Connect details
  3) Storage & secrets: KMS/HSM integration, log retention, PII redaction rules
  4) Deployment footprint: GPU sizes, expected cluster nodes, high availability zones
  5) Data ingress/egress patterns and bandwidth estimate
  6) Runbooks for security review and penetration testing
- Pilot scope example (6–8 weeks): discovery, staging deploy, validation, pilot run (production-mirroring), handover to customer ops

Premium SLA add-on play (quick pitch):
- Offer: 99.95% uptime SLA, 15 min P1 response window, priority engineering path for rollouts + quarterly architecture reviews
- Pricing levers: contract length, commit level, number of critical routes, support coverage windows (24x7)
- Customer benefits to highlight: reduced outage risk, faster incident resolution, dedicated TAM check-ins

ROI talking points & simple math (put data into customer terms):
- Example: reducing p95 latency from 1.2s -> 0.35s increases conversion by X% (customer metric). If conversion delta = 0.8% on $1M ARR, incremental revenue = $8k/mo. Compare to cost delta of dedicated pool + license.
- Cost efficiency calc: tokens_saved_per_query * avg_queries_per_month * price_per_token -> monthly saving estimate (use observed cache hit rates / batching projection)

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We don't have budget" -> Explore pilot with a time-limited usage commit or a small Dedicated pilot; present phased commitment with clear milestone metrics.
- "Security/reg reviews take too long" -> Propose a Private pilot with a scoped data plane isolation + interim compensations (audit logs, SOC2 evidence). Identify compliance rep and schedule 2-week technical deep dive.
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> Validate total cost of ownership: infra ops FTE, N+1 reliability, and dev time for model updates. Offer a benchmarking window to quantify benefits.

Renewal tracker skeleton (to paste into sheet):
Columns: Account | Renewal date | Current ARR | Passive upsell potential ($) | Primary expansion path | Decision owner | SE assigned | Technical blockers | Next milestone | Notes
Row sample: Acme Corp | 2026-04-15 | $180k | $60k | Dedicated upgrade | Sarah L. | Ravi S. | network peering | pilot kickoff 2026-02-28 | needs legal template

Pre-QBR prep checklist for CSM (action items):
- Export usage report (30/90/12mo) + token distribution by route (owner: CSM)
- Run health scan: latency, errors, model regressions (owner: SE)
- Fill qualification matrix (owner: CSM + SE)
- Draft 2 expansion propositions with high-level pricing (owner: CSM + Sales)
- Attach related tickets: security questionnaire, procurement, legal (owner: CSM)

Conversation map (short):
- If capacity signal + budget -> propose Dedicated; attach 1 pager + pilot plan
- If compliance signal strong -> propose Private pilot; map out SOC/Network owners
- If risk tolerance low but volume moderate -> propose premium SLA + observability add-on

Sample email snippets (to use after QBR):
- Quick follow-up to confirm ask:
  "Thanks for the time today — per our discussion we captured a preferred path: [Dedicated|Private|SLA]. Next steps: SE-run stage sizing (by 2026-02-22), internal legal review kickoff (by 2026-03-01). Can you confirm the decision owner?"

- Pilot kickoff invite (technical):
  "Proposed pilot plan attached: provisioning timeline, test traffic profile, rollback criteria. SE team will schedule a 60–90m technical kickoff to align on network and model artifacts."
